dedupe_keys.name: simcenter damage and loss model library dlml and dlml explorer

description: The Damage and Loss Model Library is a curated, version-controlled collection of fragility and consequence models that the NHERI SimCenter has built and maintained since 2023. It gathers the FEMA P-58 component library, Hazus building and infrastructure models, and models from the research community into one standardised format, with every model traceable to its source, and it is the default model source for SimCenter tools. The DLML Explorer, released in August 2026 with Degenkolb Engineers, is a web interface that needs no account; it lets engineers search the library in plain language, filter by hazard and source, review model parameters and metadata, and compare models. The library installs with pip install simcenter-dlml, which bundles the data and a Python API, and both are free under the BSD 3-Clause licence. Caveats: most content comes from building component libraries and Hazus, so coverage of infrastructure components depends on contributed models, and the library is growing. Coverage is not tied to one country, although FEMA P-58 and Hazus models come from the United States. It supports damage and loss simulation for hazard exposure and resilience studies; related records are Hazus and the SimCenter applications.
